title: Patient-derived Anthrobots could be deployed in vivo without an immune response

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Patient-derived Anthrobots could be deployed in vivo without an immune response

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because Anthrobots are made from adult human tissue, they could in future be personalized for each patient and deployed in that patient's body without triggering an immune response.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Anthrobots are derived from adult human tissue, and in the future could be personalized for each patient, enabling safe in‐vivo deployment of these robots in the human body without triggering an immune response.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Discussion”. Scope: Autologous Anthrobots in human patients

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-27: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.47

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Immune response and safety have clear standard endpoints. The existing in-vitro study contains none of the in-vivo autologous exposure data required to resolve the prediction.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare innate and adaptive immune activation, persistence, and pathology after autologous versus allogeneic Anthrobot administration in vivo.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No human in-vivo Anthrobot deployment data exist.

Autologous cells can still become immunogenic after culture or altered organization.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.2
operationalizability: 0.88
data adequacy: 0.08
analysis feasibility: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Immune activation and graft survival after autologous versus allogeneic placement are standard endpoints. Nothing now public is an Anthrobot implant, and graft transcriptomes in general do not substitute for that exposure. The prediction is testable and currently lacks the data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Implant Anthrobots made from a patient's own bronchial cells back into that patient, or into an autologous human explant with immune cells, and compare graft survival and T-cell or antibody responses with an allogeneic Anthrobot control. Absence of a response above the autologous-tissue baseline would support the safety claim; a raised response would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No public in vivo or immune-cell challenge of Anthrobots exists.

The statement is a future possibility, so a single negative explant would not establish clinical deployment.

Culture-expanded autologous epithelium can still be immunogenic.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.12
discriminating power: 0.34
operationalizability: 0.72
data adequacy: 0.08
analysis feasibility: 0.15
